doc: The Easter Reckoning — slot 6 of master-everyday-2 (THR-1757), the batch's appointment slot.
Two-step master Star job: reckon the true day of the Easter feast from the full moon and the
equinox, then prove it before the canons in the chapter house, with the dean answering for the
cathedral's tables. On a proved reckoning it is read before the whole synod in the chapter house
on synod day, in three days, with the dean there to answer it — an `encounter_seed` carrying an
`appointment` block (THR-1479), so the step-1 spine may name the place and time (prose rule 7b's
one lawful exception). Kept → `town.easter_reckoning_heard` (seed-only), missed →
`town.easter_reckoning_defaulted` (seed-only), both hand-authored in `easter-reckoning-sequels.ts`.
Brief: `Docs/plans/encounters/master-everyday-2-brief.md` (slot 6, binding).
Pipeline: `Docs/plans/encounters/easter-reckoning-draft.md` → `easter-reckoning-revised.md`.
plotHookRolled: hook.gods_fall, hook.prophetic_investigation, hook.builders_dilemma.
plotHookTaken: hook.prophetic_investigation — drifted: the old priests' saying that a year begun on
a false feast goes badly circulates, and the town argues whether the bad year has begun. It rides
the failure-side omen. gods_fall fought a calendar dispute (no god is gone); builders_dilemma
fought it too (nothing is built). Seed dice: p3 mystery (nobody can say whether the tables or the
priests are right) · opposition faction (doctrine: the canons hold the tables cannot be wrong) ·
disposition hostile (the canons will hear no word against the tables) · agentRole competitor (the
master's reckoning against the cathedral's own tables) · scale region (the feast day of the whole
diocese; the template field stays `local`, per the brief). Rolled setting stronghold → the
chapter house, inside the town (brief override).
─── Mechanical design block (designed before the prose) ─────────────
Crux            The cathedral's tables put this year's Easter feast a week late, and the bishop
has sent for {actor} to reckon the true day and prove it before the canons.
Whose problem?  The agent's: their reckoning, their proof, their name as the master the bishop
sent for. Scene-local; no prior tie to the cathedral asserted (rule 7).
Reach = theme?  Star throughout. Step 0 (0.74) reads the full moon and the equinox from the sky.
Step 1 (0.82) proves a reckoning of the sky against two hundred years of
copied tables. Mean 0.78, window fit 0.92 (master). Words: severe, severe.
Shape           Appointment (Seeded Sequel, placed/timed, THR-1479) on a linear two-step.
Step 0 continue_weakened; step 1 fail_action. Step 1 carries
carryoverFactorLines keyed on step 0 (no critical_failure row: a step-0
critical failure ends the action).
Consequence hand (binding, THR-1145): drive + omen — no swap.
drive         assign_ambition ambition_spread_faith on $actor, step 1 success. PATH chip.
omen          emit_omen cultural/global on step 1 success (time) and step 1 failure (entropy).
Unchipped: an omen is dressing and has no anchor kind (the restless-ossuary
precedent). Told in step 1's afterimages and the failure overview.
Appointment     step 1 success: encounter_seed templateId town.easter_reckoning_heard,
delayTicks 36, inheritContext, appointment { locationId $here, counterpartyId
$cast:dean, missed { templateId town.easter_reckoning_defaulted } }. PATH chip.
Extras          reputation_with $here +0.06 step 1 success, -0.06 step 1 failure, -0.03 step 0
failure (backs the critical_failure SCAR on the step-0 route).
Cool failure?   Nobody is hurt, jailed or branded. The cost is the master's name: the feast is
proclaimed a week late, which is what the bishop sent a master to stop.
Trait hooks     Gate: none. Variant: none — the reckoning is the sky and the sums; no live
trait reads either better than the reach does. Trait-only nudge: none.
Trait fragment: none.
Systems quota   cast (dean) · seeds (the appointment) · reputation · ambition · omen.
Cards           Step 0: Deepen The Dark (Signature, darkness), Clear The Dawn (Signature,
force) + deal 3. Step 1: Crack The Binding (Signature, entropy), Rouse The Elder
(Signature, life) + deal 3. No libraryCardId bound; no Heavy Hand; no rider.
Spheres avoid both star models and both star experts (light, time, order,
chaos, mind, spirit).
─── The narrator's 12 questions, answered ───────────────────────────
1 P1 arrival?      {actor} arrives in {location}, sent for by the bishop.
2 P2 events?       The tables set the feast for the diocese; old priests say they are a week
late; the dean keeps them and the canons will hear no word against them.
3 P3 one stake?    Mystery: nobody can say whether the tables or the priests are right.
4 ≤80 words?       Opening 9 + P2 40 + P3 27 = 76.
5 Read aloud?      Every sentence is a report.
6 Stated?          The disputed day, the dean's hold on the tables and the canons' refusal.
7 Every sentence works? Challenge, test or outcome.
8 Nothing unintroduced? The tables, the moon, the equinox, the old priests and the dean
precede step 0's cards; the copied tables and the chapter house precede
step 1's cards.
9 One named person? {cast:dean} on both spines.
10 Stake in a sentence? 'Can the bishop's master reckon the true feast day and prove it
against the cathedral's own tables, and keep their name?'
11 Cards verb+noun? Deepen, Clear, Crack, Rouse — all in the lexicon; no effect line repeats
a word of its name; no digits.
12 Opening per class? urban, the only class, written.

template.name: The Easter Reckoning

openings.urban: {actor} arrives in {location}, sent for by the bishop.

steps.narrativeTemplate:
The cathedral's tables set the day of the Easter feast for the whole diocese. This year, old priests say the tables put it a week late. The dean, {cast:dean}, keeps the tables, and the canons will hear no word against them.

The bishop asks {actor} to reckon the true day from the moon and the equinox. Nobody in {location} can say whether the tables or the priests are right.
steps.criticalSuccessAfterimage: They fixed the equinox to the morning and the full moon to the hour, and the true feast falls a week before the tables' day.
steps.successAfterimage: They fixed the equinox and the full moon after it, and the true feast falls a week before the tables' day.
steps.successAtCostAfterimage: They fixed the true day, a week before the tables' day, but the dean's clerks saw them on the cathedral tower at night.
steps.failureAfterimage: Cloud hid the full moon, and they could say only that the tables might be a week out.
steps.criticalFailureAfterimage: They reckoned the full moon a night early, and the dean's clerks wrote the mistake down.

nudges.name: Deepen The Dark
nudges.effectLine: Put out every lamp in the cathedral close tonight, so the moon's edge and the faint stars show plainly.

bandProse.critical_success: Every lamp in the close went out, and the moon rose clear of the roofs to its full.
bandProse.success: The lamps in the close went out, and the edge of the full moon showed plainly.
bandProse.near_miss: The lamps went out, but a tavern fire kept the low sky bright.
bandProse.failure: The lamps went out, and cloud came over the moon anyway.

nudges.name: Clear The Dawn
nudges.effectLine: Drive the haze off the eastern hills at sunrise, so the morning the sun rises straight down the cathedral's aisle shows plainly.

bandProse.success_at_cost: The haze lifted at sunrise, and the sun rose straight down the aisle while the dean's sexton watched.
bandProse.failure: The haze lifted, but the sun rose behind the bell tower and could not be read.
bandProse.critical_failure: The haze lifted a day too soon, and they took the wrong morning for the equinox.

steps.narrativeTemplate: The canons meet in the chapter house to hear the reckoning. {cast:dean} answers for the cathedral's tables, which have been copied from book to book for two hundred years, and says a copy that old cannot be wrong. If {actor} proves the reckoning, it is read before the whole synod in the chapter house on synod day, in three days, with the dean there to answer it. If not, {location} will think less of {actor}.
steps.criticalSuccessAfterimage: The canons checked every row of the tables against the reckoning, and asked {actor} to stand beside them at the synod.
steps.successAfterimage: The canons checked the reckoning against the tables row by row, and agreed the synod must hear it.
steps.successAtCostAfterimage: The canons agreed the synod must hear it, but {cast:dean} told the bishop that {actor} had shamed the chapter.
steps.failureAfterimage: The canons would not see the fault, and {cast:dean} had the tables read out as they stand.
steps.criticalFailureAfterimage: {cast:dean} found an error in {actor}'s own sums and read it out to the canons.

critical_success.text: They can name the hour of the full moon.

success.text: They know the true feast falls a week early.

success_at_cost.text: The dean knows they read the sky from the cathedral tower.

near_miss.text: They know the full moon only to the night.

failure.text: They can say only that the tables might be wrong.

effects.narrativeHook: Proved the cathedral's feast tables a week wrong before the canons, and means every parish to keep the true day.
A master proved a cathedral's feast tables a week wrong, and the town began to say the year will go well if the feast is kept on its true day.

effects.seedLabel: The reckoning is read before the synod in the chapter house on synod day, with the dean there to answer it.

missed.seedLabel: The reckoning was not read on synod day, and the dean comes looking for the master who made it.

effects.narrativeHook: A cathedral will keep the Easter feast a week late, the old priests say a year begun on a false feast goes badly, and the town argues whether the bad year has begun.

nudges.name: Crack The Binding
nudges.effectLine: Split the spine of the dean's copy of the tables, so its loose leaves show where a copyist skipped a line.

bandProse.critical_success: The dean's copy split at the spine, and the leaf with the skipped line fell open in front of the canons.
bandProse.success: The old spine split, and the canons saw where a copyist had skipped a line.
bandProse.near_miss: The old spine split, but the dean gathered up the loose leaves before the canons read them.
bandProse.failure: The old spine split, and the dean blamed the damp in the chapter house.

nudges.name: Rouse The Elder
nudges.effectLine: Give the oldest of the doubting priests the strength to climb the chapter house stair and speak.

bandProse.success_at_cost: The oldest priest climbed the stair and spoke for the reckoning, and the dean sent him back to his parish for it.
bandProse.failure: The oldest priest climbed the stair, but his voice was too weak to carry across the chapter house.
bandProse.critical_failure: The oldest priest climbed the stair and could not remember which year the tables went wrong.
